notes.text: These are the generations of Jacob — It is not a barren genealogy, as those of Esau, but a memorable useful history. Joseph brought to his father their evil report - Jacob's sons did that when they were from under his eye, which they durst not have done if they had been at home with him; but Joseph gave his father an account of their ill carriage, that he might reprove and restrain them.
He made him a coat of divers colours — Which probably was significant of farther honours intended him.

glossa.text:
« Joseph, when he was sixteen years old, » etc., ((AUG. in Q. super Genesin. )) *Historically.* How can the death of Isaac, etc., *as far as* yet in Isaac's lifetime Joseph began to be seventeen years old.

« And he was with the sons of Bala, » etc. Joseph, one of the twelve sons of Jacob, beloved of his father beyond the rest, signified Christ, whom, born according to the flesh, God the Father preferred to the rest of the brethren begotten of the stock of Abraham. Whence Jacob loved him, « because he had begotten him in his old age. » For when the world was growing old, the Son of God was born of the Virgin, as it were a son of old age.

« And he was with, » etc. In the primitive Church he did not cast off those who clave to him through the preaching of false apostles, whom the handmaids of Jacob signify, whom also he would not forbid, when they wrought miracles in his name.

« And he made him a coat of divers colours. » ((HIER.)) For *a parti-coloured tunic* Aquila has rendered ἀστραγάλον, that is, *reaching to the ankles,* Symmachus *sleeved,* either because it came down as far as the ankles and was marked out with a wonderful variety by the craftsman's hands, or because it had sleeves: for the ancients used rather colobia, that is, garments without sleeves.

((GREG., hom. XXV in Evang.)) Because Joseph is described as having persevered just among his brethren to the end of his life, he alone is said to have had a coat reaching to the ankles. What is a coat reaching to the ankles, but a completed action? For as it were a coat stretched down covered the ankle of the body, when a good action rules us before the eyes of God to the bounds of life. Whence Moses commanded the tail of the victim to be offered, that we may complete with a persevering end the good work which we begin.

« And his brethren seeing, » etc. The brethren of Christ according to the flesh are the Jews, of whose kindred he took flesh. But because they saw that the grace of virtues was wrought in him, which bore witness to the Father's especial love, they envied him, and could not speak anything peaceably to him, and again and again attempted snares, and blasphemously said that the Master of the household cast out demons by Beelzebub the prince of demons.

((ISID.)) This was spiritually fulfilled in Christ, etc., *as far as* in the figure of the stars.

notes.text: Glory — Glory in the God whom you serve, as the only true God.
Seek — The Lord in his strength, in his sanctuary, or before the ark, which is called God's strength. Face - His gracious presence.
Judgments — The punishments which he brought upon Egypt by his mere word.
Of Jacob — The only branch of Abraham's seed to whom the following blessings belong.

glossa.text:
*Alleluia.* ((CASS.)) Here for the first time *alleluia,* nor was it set down before this by anyone; and no tongue has presumed to change it. *Alleluia,* praise ye. *Ia* is the name of the invisible God, which belongs to him alone. Through twenty psalms, which have this title, the great works of God are told, and great is the exultation in them. ((CASS.)) Here the prophet commends the good among that people of Israel, who together with other believers are the true seed of Abraham, the children of the promise.

*Give glory to the Lord.* ((AUG.)) The first psalm to which alleluia is prefixed, etc., *as far as* he subjoins what temporal things the mercy of God gave them.
*All things:* ((CASS.)) all things; there is nothing that shame should keep silent. Or, all the things which they shall tell are wonderful, for no one can relate them all.

*Be ye praised in the name,* that is, rejoice that you are called Christians from Christ.

((AUG.)) Be ye praised: he does not forbid being praised, if they are good; if they are not, then not save in the Lord, who makes men good. Be ye praised in the name. Which elsewhere is, *In the Lord shall my soul be praised:* what he adds there, *let the meek hear and rejoice:* here too in a manner, *let the heart rejoice,* as if he should say,

*The face,* etc. ((ID.)) That is, the presence, etc., *as far as* the wicked man can fear the presence which the good man loves. ((HIER.)) From the martyr Hippolytus, etc., *as far as* there about to take his Church from among the Gentiles.

*Remember, and the rest.* ((AUG.)) Seek him, etc., *as far as* if it is a great thing to seek what God is, at least behold the things which he has made. *The wonders,* etc. ((ID.)) Little by little he ascends from visible wonders to judgments: thence to the everlasting testament, where there is both precept and promise.

notes.text: For Moses describeth the only righteousness which is attainable by the law, when he saith, The man who doeth these things shall live by them — that is, he that perfectly keeps all these precepts in every point, he alone may claim life and salvation by them. But this way of justification is impossible to any who have ever transgressed any one law in any point. Lev. xviii, 5

But the righteousness which is by faith — The method of becoming righteous by believing. Speaketh a very different language, and may be considered as expressing itself thus: (to accommodate to our present subject the words which Moses spake, touching the plainness of his law:) Say not in thy heart, Who shall ascend into heaven, as if it were to bring Christ down: or, Who shall descend into the grave, as if it were to bring him again from the dead - Do not imagine that these things are to be done now, in order to procure thy pardon and salvation. Deut. xxx, 14.

But what saith he — Moses. Even these words, so remarkably applicable to the subject before us. All is done ready to thy hand. The word is nigh thee - Within thy reach; easy to be understood, remembered, practiced. This is eminently true of the word of faith - The gospel. Which we preach - The sum of which is, If thy heart believe in Christ, and thy life confess him, thou shalt be saved.
If thou confess with thy mouth — Even in time of persecution, when such a confession may send thee to the lions.

For with the heart — Not the understanding only. Man believeth to righteousness - So as to obtain justification. And with the mouth confession is made - So as to obtain final salvation. Confession here implies the whole of outward, as believing does the root of all inward, religion.
Isaiah xxviii, 16.

The same Lord of all is rich — So that his blessings are never to be exhausted, nor is he ever constrained to hold his hand. The great truth proposed in ver. 11 is so repeated here, and in ver. 13, and farther confirmed, ver. 14, 15, as not only to imply, that "whosoever calleth upon him shall be saved;" but also that the will of God is, that all should savingly call upon him.
Joel ii, 32.

But how shall they preach, unless they be sent — Thus by a chain of reasoning, from God's will that the gentiles also should "call upon him," St. Paul infers that the apostles were sent by God to preach to the gentiles also. The feet - Their very footsteps; their coming. Isaiah lii, 7.

glossa.text: *He shall live in it.* He has this reward, namely that he be not punished by that death. But it is no great justice to fear, nor has it merit with God.
*That is, to bring Christ down.* That is, to deny that Christ has ascended.

*The word is nigh.* That is, it is useful, or there is nothing unfitting either to say or to believe. Or *nigh,* because it is not far from the nature of minds: and by the manner of speaking, that which is said to us that we may believe.

*This is the word. ((AUG., Tract. 80, in Joannem.))* Of which the Lord says: *For you are clean by reason of the word which I have spoken to you,* etc. *as far as* for in the word itself one thing is the sound that passes, another the power that remains.

*That if thou confess. ((AUG.))* Behold the praise of faith and its reward. The praise of faith is, if thou shalt have believed that Jesus is Lord, etc., *as far as* who goes before it in a resurrection suited to itself, that is, in justification.

*With the heart we believe.* Other things a man can do unwilling, but he cannot believe save willing.

*Confession. ((AUG., in Psal. XXX, concione III.))* To confess is to say what is in the heart, etc., *as far as* because he so believes, so also he ought in the mouth, that he may so preach.

*Who call upon him.* He that prays calls upon; but this assuredly he cannot do, unless he first believe. They therefore who call upon him not only believe, but also pray, so that after anyone's mind has believed it may not cease to ask that which God promised to them that watch with the whole heart, because to believe gives the remission of sins. But to call upon obtains the promises of God.

*How then shall they call upon,* etc. It being proved that this is taken of both peoples, he shows through what, namely through the mission made to both, which he who shall not have received is inexcusable. Invocation saves, therefore one must believe: because, *how,* etc. *Or how shall they believe,* etc. As if he should say: They will not believe, unless they hear. For neither did anyone of old believe who did not in some manner hear, either inwardly or outwardly. But he says that to believe is of hearing, to hear of preaching, to preach of the mission of God; so that the whole comes down from the fount of grace. But preaching truly is of a mission, because God, who knows how to use evil unto good, sent even false men that announce good things. Sometimes also he sends the evil to the evil in wrath, that is, he permits evil men to preach to evil men for the punishment of the same, that by turns through themselves, as is just, they may perish.

((AUG.)) What the Apostle says: *How shall they believe him whom they have not heard?* he said of the Gentiles, etc., *as far as* that preachers of Christ are to be sent.

*But how shall they preach unless they be sent?* Behold, it appears that preachers were sent to the Gentiles also. *How beautiful.* Because they enlighten the world, wherein it appears that they were sent by God, otherwise they could not do this. *Peace.* Reconciliation between people and people, the wall of the legal rite among the Jews, and of idolatry among the Gentiles, being broken down. And between God, justifying the ungodly through faith, and men believing in him. *Of them that bring glad tidings of good things.* Peace upon peace, because the kingdom of God also is peace.

notes.text: He constrained his disciples — Who were unwilling to leave him. Mark vi, 45; John vi, 15.
In the evening — Learned men say the Jews reckoned two evenings; the first beginning at three in the afternoon, the second, at sunset. If so, the latter is meant here.

The fourth watch — The Jews (as well as the Romans) usually divided the night into four watches, of three hours each. The first watch began at six, the second at nine, the third at twelve, the fourth at three in the morning. If it be thou - It is the same as, Since it is thou. The particle if frequently bears this meaning, both in ours and in all languages. So it means, John xiii, 14, 17. St. Peter was in no doubt, or he would not have quitted the ship.
He was afraid — Though he had been used to the sea, and was a skilful swimmer. But so it frequently is. When grace begins to act, the natural courage and strength are withdrawn.
Thou art the Son of God — They mean, the Messiah.

glossa.text: *He went up.* He fed the crowd as God, he went up to pray as man. Not as one not having all things in his power, but that he might fulfil the form of a man. In this there is a duty of piety; there follows a notable miracle of power. *And when it was evening.* Rightly is this storm said to be in the evening, because while the Church is in tribulation, she is said to be as it were in the night, and the sun of justice seems to have hidden himself.

*But the boat.* The ship in the midst of the sea, Jesus alone on the land: because sometimes the Church is so, not only afflicted but also defiled, that she seems utterly forsaken by God: but God does not forsake her. Whence Mark says: *He saw them labouring in rowing ((Marc. VI))* . Though not present, and though he defers, yet he sees and strengthens.

*And in the fourth.* They are in peril the whole night, because when a man considers himself, he finds nothing but the darkness of straits and the surgings of enemies.

*He came to them.* Mark says: *Willing to pass by them,* for whose deliverance nevertheless he came. Which happens so that, being troubled for an hour but soon delivered, they may wonder the more, and give thanks; which same thing often happens in the passions of the saints.

*And seeing him,* etc. Because it often happens that when some sudden abatement of a long tribulation arises, it is not straightway believed to be a true deliverance. And therefore, the former dread remaining intense , prayer is directed toward deliverance.
*It is I, fear ye not.* He does not add who, because from the voice known to them they could recognize him. Or because he himself is he who said: *He who is hath sent me to you ((Exod. III))*.
*Lord, if it be thou.* If thou art that deliverer, bid me come to the imitation of thee by overcoming pressures.

*And going down.* Despairing of human help, he treads down pressures with his mind, that he may be conformed to Jesus. *He walked,* etc. Behold, a man walks upon the waters. Doubt not therefore that Christ is a true body, because he walked upon the waters.

He made him walk upon the sea, that he might show the divine power. He makes him sink, lest he forget his infirmity, lest he think himself equal to God, and lest he grow proud.

*And when he had begun,* etc. He is left a little to temptation, that faith may be increased; for as he believed that by his command he could be upheld upon the waves, so, while he sinks, that he could be saved by his power.
*The wind ceased.* In whomsoever God is present by grace, straightway all wars grow quiet.
*And they adored him,* etc. The sign being seen, they confess him the Son of God: why then should Arius bring it about that he is a creature?

notes.text: Unto a cave — Perhaps the same wherein Moses was hid when the Lord passed before him, and proclaimed his name.

I have been, &c. — I have executed my office with zeal for God's honour, and with the hazard of my own life, and am fled hither, not being able to endure to see the dishonour done to thy name by their obstinate idolatry and wickedness. I only - Of all thy prophets, who boldly and publickly plead thy cause: for the rest of thy prophets who are not slain, hide themselves, and dare not appear to do thee any service. They seek my life - I despair of doing them any good: for instead of receiving my testimony, they hunt for my life. It does by no means appear, that he was at all to blame, for fleeing from Jezebel. If they persecute you in one city flee into another. Besides, the angels feeding and preparing him for his journey, and the peculiar blessing of God upon that food, indicated the divine approbation.

And behold — This is a general description of the thing, after which the manner of it is particularly explained. Strong wind - Whereby he both prepares Elijah to receive this discovery of God with greatest humility, reverence, and godly fear; and signifies his irresistible power, to break the hardest hearts of the Israelites, and to bear down all opposition that was or should be made against him in the discharge of his office. The Lord was not - The Lord did not vouchsafe his special and gracious presence to Elijah in that wind, which possibly was to teach him not to wonder if God did not accompany his terrible administration at mount Carmel with the presence of his grace, to turn the hearts of the Israelites to himself.

A still voice — To intimate, that God would do his work in and for Israel in his own time, not by might or power, but by his own spirit, Zech iv, 6, which moves with a powerful, but yet with a sweet and gentle gale.

He wrapped, &c. — Through dread of God's presence, being sensibly that he was neither worthy nor able to endure the sight of God with open face. And stood, &c. - Which God commanded him to do; and as he was going towards the mouth of the cave, he was affrighted and stopped in his course, by the dreadful wind, and earthquake, and fire; when these were past, he prosecutes his journey, and goeth on to the mouth of the cave.

The son, &c. — That is, his grand-son, for he was the son of Jehosaphat, 2 Kings ix, 2. This was intended as a prediction that by these God would punish the degenerate Israelites, plead his own cause among them, and avenge the quarrel of his covenant.

Shall Elisha slay — One or other of these should infallibly execute God's judgments upon the apostate Israelites. Elisha is said to slay them, either, because he slew those forty two children, 2 Kings ii, 24, besides others whom upon like occasions he might destroy; or, because he by God's appointment inflicted the famine, 2 Kings viii, 1, or rather, by the sword which came out of his mouth: the prophets being said to pull down and to destroy what they declare and foretel shall be pulled down. Hazael began to slay them before Jehu was king, though his cruelty was much increased afterward. Jehu destroyed those whom Hazael did not, as king Joram himself, and Ahaziah, and all the near relations of Ahab.

I have left — Or, I have reserved to myself; I have kept from the common contagion: therefore thou art mistaken to think that thou art left alone. Seven thousand - Either, definitely so many: or rather, indefinitely, for many thousands; the number of seven being often used for a great number. Kissed him - That is, all those who have not worshipped Baal, nor professed reverence or subjection to him: which idolaters did to their idols, by bowing the knee, and by kissing them.

glossa.text:
*And a wind.* ((ID.)) A wind before the Lord overthrows mountains and breaks rocks in pieces, etc., *as far as* to begin to go forth to the knowledge of the truth.

*Not in the wind.* That is, think not that the Lord comes with the wind, but after the wind of commotion, that is, the whirlwind and the rush of the wind, fire shall pass by, then a whistling of a thin air, after this the Lord shall pass by, that he may speak with thee.

*I only,* etc. ((RAB.)) What was hard for so great a prophet to know, that servants had remained to God in this world? But he who, being humble, had known even the hidden things of God, being lifted up knew not even the open things. Whence it is certain that he enlightens himself with a ray of humility who subtly weighs the good things of others: because while he beholds outwardly, and in others, the things which he himself has done, he presses down that swelling of pride which strives to break forth within out of singularity. Hence it is that by the voice of God it is said to Elias, who reckoned himself alone. *I have left me seven thousand men,* that while he knew that not he alone had remained, he might bow down the glory of elation which was rising in him out of singularity.

((RAB.)) Not otherwise, save that he foretold that he should be king. Eliseus not otherwise than by casting his mantle upon him. Those two kings neither he himself in person, nor Eliseus his disciple, anointed, but a certain one of the prophets was sent to anoint Jehu.
*Whosoever.* ((ID.)) The guilty, divine justice makes some to be punished by kings with the sword, others it pierces through by prophets and priests with the sword of the tongue.

notes.text: Will hear — Diligently observe. Will speak - What answer God will give to my prayers. Peace - He will give an answer of peace. Saints - Not to all that are called God's people, but only to those who are truly such.

His salvation — That compleat salvation for which all the Israel of God wait; even the redemption by the Messiah; of which not only Christian, but even Jewish writers understand this place; and to which the following passages properly belong. And the psalmist might well say this salvation was nigh, because the seventy weeks determined by Daniel were begun. Glory - The glorious presence of God, and the God of glory himself, even Christ, who is the brightness of his father's glory.

Kissed — That great work of redemption by Christ, shall clearly manifest God's mercy in redeeming his people Israel, and in the conversion of the Gentiles; his truth in fulfilling that great promise of sending his son, his righteousness in punishing sin, on his son, and in conferring righteousness upon guilty and lost creatures; and his peace or reconciliation to sinners, and that peace of conscience which attends upon it.
Truth — Truth among men. Righteousness - And God's justice shall be satisfied: he shall look down upon sinful men with a smiling countenance.

Before him — As his harbinger. He shall fulfil all righteousness, he shall satisfy the righteousness of God, and shall advance righteousness and holiness among men. Set us - Shall cause us to walk in those righteous ways wherein he walketh. David prays for the favour and blessing of God, ver. 1-6. Expresses confidence in him, by praise mingled with prayer, ver. 7-17. A prayer of David.

glossa.text: *I will hear what the Lord speaketh in me.* ((CASS.)) Whence he knows, and by whom it is done, and what he himself bestows in coming. *Peace.* ((AUG.)) Christ. Peace toward God and toward the neighbour, and through Christ.
*Near them that fear him.* ((ID.)) Everywhere demons were worshipped, etc., *as far as* immortal in our body now mortal.
*Mercy,* etc. ((ID.)) After he had said, etc., *as far as how truth is sprung out of the earth ((Luc. VIII))*.
*Truth is sprung out of the earth.* ((ID.)) Confession from man, that he may accuse himself, etc., *as far as* the justification of him that confesses is given.

*Justice shall go before him.* ((ID.)) The first justice of man is, etc., *as far as* and visiting he shall set his steps in the way. *Shall walk.* It shall increase, or shall run before, preparing the way for him; and the Lord shall set his steps in the way made ready.

*And going down.* Despairing of human help, he treads down pressures with his mind, that he may be conformed to Jesus. *He walked,* etc. Behold, a man walks upon the waters. Doubt not therefore that Christ is a true body, because he walked upon the waters.

He made him walk upon the sea, that he might show the divine power. He makes him sink, lest he forget his infirmity, lest he think himself equal to God, and lest he grow proud.

*And when he had begun,* etc. He is left a little to temptation, that faith may be increased; for as he believed that by his command he could be upheld upon the waves, so, while he sinks, that he could be saved by his power.
*The wind ceased.* In whomsoever God is present by grace, straightway all wars grow quiet.
*And they adored him,* etc. The sign being seen, they confess him the Son of God: why then should Arius bring it about that he is a creature?

registers.label: Spare
lines: The boat was far from land, beaten by the waves.
And out of the storm Jesus came walking.
Peter stepped down, then saw the wind and began to sink.
Lord, save me — and at once the hand reached out.
Take heart, says Jesus; it is I, do not be afraid.
We come out of the storm to you.
Come, let us worship the God who holds us up.
We come; do not let us go. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Feel the boat pitch in the dark, the wind against you, the water cold and rising and no shore in sight.
Take heart; do not be afraid.
Then a figure on the waves, and a voice over the storm you half remember from somewhere safe: it is I.
Take heart; do not be afraid.
Peter climbed out onto the water, then felt the wind, and the moment he doubted, he began to go under.
Take heart; do not be afraid.
But the hand was faster than the wave — Jesus caught him, and the same hand reaches for you.
Take heart; do not be afraid. He will not let us sink!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The boat was beaten far from shore in the dark.
Take heart; do not be afraid.
Across the waves Jesus came: it is I.
Take heart; do not be afraid.
Peter sank, and at once the hand reached out.
Take heart; do not be afraid.
Come, let us worship the God who holds us up.
Take heart; do not be afraid. Amen.

turn.gravity: Joseph is sold into a pit by his own brothers in the wilderness (Genesis 37); the Psalm recalls how God led Joseph, "bound in fetters," until the appointed word came to pass (Psalm 105); Paul insists faith comes only by a word that must first be sent and heard (Romans 10); and Peter steps out onto the sea and sinks the moment he looks at the wind. The nerve: faith is tested exactly in the gap between the word that calls and the ground giving way beneath it.
turn.trap: Becomes a self-help parable ("keep your eyes on Jesus, not the waves") or a shame-story about Peter's "little faith" — missing that Jesus comes walking toward them in the storm before Peter asks anything, and catches him the instant he calls.
turn.hinge: He rebukes Peter's "little faith" — but it was a little faith that got him out of the boat and walking on water in the first place, more than the other eleven managed.

doors.claim: Jesus walks toward the disciples in their fourth-watch panic before any of them asks for help — the initiative is his, not Peter's daring.

witnesses.author: Augustine
witnesses.reading: The Lord came to visit His disciples who are tossed on the sea in the fourth watch of the night — that is, at its close.

witnesses.author: John Chrysostom
witnesses.reading: Christ then did not reveal Himself to His disciples until they cried out; for the more intense their fear, the more did they rejoice in His presence.

doors.say: He was already walking toward the boat before anyone in it knew to hope for him.
doors.do: Ask them to name the storm they assume they're facing alone, and name whose feet are already on the water.

doors.claim: Peter's faith is real even though it falters — he asks to do the very thing Christ is doing, and is answered.

witnesses.author: John Chrysostom
witnesses.reading: See how great his warmth, how great his faith. He said not, Pray and entreat for me; but 'Bid me.'

witnesses.author: Augustine
witnesses.reading: This I am not able by myself, but in Thee I am able. Peter confessed what he was in himself, and what he should receive from Him.

doors.say: Peter didn't ask Jesus to calm the sea for him — he asked to walk on it with him. That is faith, not presumption.
doors.do: Have them name one impossible thing they've stopped asking for because it seemed presumptuous, and ask again.

doors.claim: The sinking is not the end of the story — Christ's hand is faster than Peter's fear.

witnesses.author: John Chrysostom
witnesses.reading: He bade not the winds to cease, but stretched forth His hand and caught him, because his faith was required.

witnesses.author: Rabanus Maurus
witnesses.reading: The Lord looked back upon him, and brought him to repentance; He stretched forth His hand, and forgave him, and thus the disciple found salvation.

doors.say: He did not still the wind first — he caught Peter first. The rescue came before the calm.
doors.do: Ask them to recall a moment they were caught mid-fall, and name whose hand it was.

synthesis.convergence: Joseph is dragged into a storm not of his making, and God is present in the pit before Joseph can see it (Genesis 37; Psalm 105); Paul insists faith comes only by a word that must first be sent and heard (Romans 10); Peter steps onto chaos and does not drown because a hand is already reaching. Every reading agrees: God is present in the crisis before you can name it, calling by a word that precedes your faith.
synthesis.claim: The storm did not start when you noticed it — Christ was already walking toward you across it.
synthesis.here: For people paralyzed by "not enough faith," don't demand more faith — point at whose hand is already extended. Their little faith is what got them out of the boat, and it is enough to be caught.

turn.subtract: Three landings — Christ's initiative, Peter's daring ask, or the catching hand. Choose one and let the others go.
